_readme: Reference context and personal goals for `health`. This public template deliberately ships with no personal goals: age, sex, pregnancy, disability, altitude, medication, diagnosis, device accuracy, and the user's own priorities can all change what is appropriate. `ref` is included only where the linked source supports a broadly applicable adult resting range. Add goal_min or goal_max yourself after deciding what is right for you. This file is educational context, not diagnosis or medical advice.

RestingHeartRate.label: Resting HR
RestingHeartRate.why: The American Heart Association says 60-100 bpm is normal for most adults and that physically active adults may be as low as 40 bpm. Symptoms, medication and medical history matter more than this broad screen.

HeartRate.label: Heart rate (all-day avg)
HeartRate.why: An all-day average mixes rest, exercise and missing wear time, so a resting clinical range does not apply. Use the personal trend and RestingHeartRate instead.

HeartRateVariabilitySDNN.label: HRV (SDNN)
HeartRateVariabilitySDNN.why: HRV depends strongly on age, measurement duration, posture, device and the individual. This template does not turn a population distribution into a personal threshold.

OxygenSaturation.label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
OxygenSaturation.why: The FDA says 95-100% is typical for most healthy people, while altitude, circulation, skin pigmentation, temperature and device limitations affect readings. Do not diagnose or change treatment from a watch reading alone.

RespiratoryRate.label: Respiratory rate
RespiratoryRate.why: MedlinePlus lists 12-18 breaths per minute as a normal resting adult vital-sign range. This does not apply during exercise and should not replace clinical assessment.

StepCount.label: Daily steps
StepCount.why: Large cohort studies associate more daily steps with lower mortality, but they do not establish one universal daily prescription. Pick a goal relative to your baseline, mobility and clinician's advice.

AppleExerciseTime.label: Exercise minutes
AppleExerciseTime.why: WHO guidance is weekly: adults should generally get at least 150 minutes of moderate activity, or 75 minutes vigorous, plus muscle strengthening. A daily goal can misrepresent that weekly recommendation.

AppleStandHour.label: Stand hours
AppleStandHour.why: This is an Apple ring measure, not a universal clinical threshold. Set a personal goal only if the ring is useful for breaking up your own sedentary time.

TimeInDaylight.label: Daylight
TimeInDaylight.why: HealthKit records exposure time, but this template does not prescribe a universal daily target.

DistanceWalkingRunning.label: Walk+run distance
DistanceWalkingRunning.why: Distance depends on stride length, mobility and activity type. It is best treated as a personal trend rather than a population target.

SleepHours.label: Time asleep
SleepHours.why: AASM and Sleep Research Society recommend that adults generally sleep 7 or more hours per night. They did not set a universal upper limit, and sleep need varies, so this public template leaves the goal unset. min_days avoids judging a sparse or stale watch record.

BodyMass.label: Weight
BodyMass.why: No universal target is meaningful without height, body composition, health history and the individual's goals. Track the trend only unless you set a personal range.

BodyFatPercentage.label: Body fat
BodyFatPercentage.why: Interpretation varies by sex, age, device and clinical context. The public template intentionally has no male or female default.

VO2Max.label: VO2 max
VO2Max.why: Reference values vary substantially by age, sex, protocol and device estimation. Compare against an appropriate source or clinician before adding a goal.

WalkingHeartRateAverage.label: Walking HR
WalkingHeartRateAverage.why: There is no universal cutoff for an all-walking average. Pace, terrain, temperature, medication and fitness all affect it; use comparable personal trends.

AppleWalkingSteadiness.label: Walking steadiness
AppleWalkingSteadiness.why: This is an Apple-derived mobility classification, not a general percentage target. Interpret it through Apple's Health app and clinical context.

HeadphoneAudioExposure.label: Headphone audio
HeadphoneAudioExposure.why: WHO safe-listening guidance combines loudness and duration: for example, 80 dB for up to 40 hours per week. A daily average alone cannot represent dose, so no simple range is configured.

EnvironmentalAudioExposure.label: Environment audio
EnvironmentalAudioExposure.why: Hearing risk depends on both level and exposure duration. This daily average is useful for trend inspection but is not a complete exposure-dose calculation.

FlightsClimbed.label: Flights climbed
FlightsClimbed.why: No universal clinical guideline is configured. Treat it as a personal incidental-activity trend.

ActiveEnergyBurned.label: Active energy
ActiveEnergyBurned.why: The estimate depends on body metrics, device calibration and activity type. No population target is meaningful here.

BasalEnergyBurned.label: Basal energy
BasalEnergyBurned.why: This is a device estimate from body metrics rather than a direct measurement. Use it to notice discontinuities, not as a goal.

systems._readme: Groups for the coverage matrix. They show which kinds of data exist in each year; absence is not a medical finding.
